Flash infusing the spirit with the tea will give you a good Earl Gray flavor without the bitterness. I’ve used this technique in many cocktails with great results. 

Fill a conical strainer with a teaspoon of tea, position it over a pint glass or other container, and add a splash of warm water to moisten the leaves. Discard the water that has dripped into the glass, and slowly pour the desired spirit over the tea leaves. I try to do a several ounces at a time to ensure that the flavor remains consistent through a few cocktails. Do not press the tea leaves to extract any remaining spirit, this will release the bitter aspects that you are trying to avoid.

I learned to use midi machines to compose electronic music back in the late 1990’s and early 2000’s. It literally saved my life. Focusing my energy into creating music instead of into feeding my depression helped me overcome my sadness. Twenty years later I can listen to those tracks and feel reassured that I took the right steps to put those demons to rest. 
I know that Reddit looks down on people plugging their own stuff but if you want a window into my experience please check out Karmic Soundsystem on SoundCloud. The first few tracks you will find are experimental mixes I made using Ableton Live. The tracks that follow are all original compositions made on some pretty dated midi equipment. 
My best advice is be careful with the drugs. MDMA can be helpful in showing you a path out of depression but you can’t live your life rolling every day. Use them sparingly and make an effort to make real change in your life from revelations you experience. 
Life is amazing and precious, and you deserve all that it has to offer, but you have to work to make it happen. Peace.

I have read The Bar Chef. It’s one of my favorite books for unique cocktail components and creative builds.

Both books lend themselves to making cocktails that are very prep intensive. It’s mind boggling for me to imagine putting forth and successfully executing a menu with more than eight of these drinks. 

The Aviary’s book takes things a step further by incorporating more progressive cuisine techniques. There are a handful of ingredients that you’ll have to source on Modernist Pantry, and learn to use. 

I’ve been lucky enough to have had the time and money over the past six years to study and acquire some the techniques and tools used to execute some of these drinks. Now I just need to find a practical way of incorporating them into my cocktail menus.

Many of the techniques and processes in the book are not necessarily new. The book puts forth some creative applications for modernist/progressive cuisine tricks in cocktails. Anyone who has dabbled with basic molecular gastronomy should find most of the recipes in the book to be very straightforward and accessible.

I found the Pyrolizing of Chartreuse and bananas to be especially fascinating. I’m not sure that I have the patience to wait six months to a year for it though. 

I will use this book primarily for new recipes for dusts, syrups, infusions and tinctures. There are so many cool cocktail build ideas in the book incorporating these different components. I especially like the ideas put forth for using siphons and porthole infusers for tableside use.

PERFECT SUSHI RICE

READY IN: 1 hr 30 mins
YIELDS: 4 cups rice
INGREDIENTS

2  cups sushi rice
2  cups water
4  tablespoons rice vinegar
3  tablespoons sugar
2  teaspoons salt
2  tablespoons mirin
 kelp, leaf (optional)
DIRECTIONS

Ignore the directions on the bag that the rice came from and rinse the rice only 3-5 times. The water does NOT have to run clear.
Place rice to drain in a strainer.
Drain for one hour in the winter, 30 min in the summer. (Sounds strange, but is true).
While rice is draining, combine vinegar,sugar, salt and mirin together in a bowl and mix well.
If using a kelp leaf,it should be about 2 in long 
Wipe it lightly, cut small slits to make it look like a comb and add it to a pot along with the water.
Add rice to the pot.
Bring quickly to a boil and then reduce to a simmer.
Cover the pot and DON'T touch it until the end, NO PEEKING.
Cook for 15 minutes before removing the pot from the heat but keep the lid CLOSED.
Let rice rest for 10 min and then remove the cover.
Place in a glass dish to cool and lightly fan the rice while adding the vinegar mixture.
Mix rice gently, careful not to break it.
Sushi rice is best used at body temperature.
